questions.question: In terms of area, which state has the largest forest cover in India?
questions.solution:
In terms of **area**, __**Madhya Pradesh**__ has the **largest forest cover in India.**

__
 
• It is the second-largest state by area after Rajasthan in India, and the **fifth-largest state by population.**
 
• The capital of Madhya Pradesh is **Bhopal.**
 
• The largest city of Madhya Pradesh is **Indore.**
 
• As per the economy, it is the **10th largest state economy in India.**

**Notes:**

 
• Area-wise **Madhya Pradesh**__ has the largest forest cover in the country followed by **Arunachal Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha,** and **Maharashtra**.

questions.question: With which country does India share the longest border?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bangladesh.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The India-Bangladesh border:-**

 
 
• India shares the longest border with Bangladesh, which is approximately 4,096 km long.
 
• It is also known as the** International Border (IB)** and is divided into three sectors, namely,** Eastern, Central, and Western.**
 
• The India-Bangladesh border is characterized by numerous** rivers and their tributaries**, which act as natural boundaries between the two countries.
 
• The border is also marked by **fencing, pillars, and barbed wires **to prevent illegal immigration, smuggling, and other cross-border crimes.
 
• The India-Bangladesh border is of **strategic importance** to both countries as it connects the northeastern states of India with the rest of the country and provides Bangladesh with access to the** Bay of Bengal.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **China** shares a border with India, which is approximately **3,488 km long.**

 
 
• The India-China border is also known as the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)** and is the subject of a** long-standing territorial dispute** between the two countries.
 
 
 
• **Nepal** shares a border with India, which is approximately **1,751 km long.**
 
 
• The** India-Nepal border **is open and free for **movement of people and goods**.
 
 
 
• **Pakistan **shares a border with India, which is approximately **3,323 km long.**
 
 
• The India-Pakistan border is also known as the** Line of Control (LoC) **and is heavily militarized due to the **ongoing conflict **between the two countries over the disputed region of Kashmir.

questions.question: What is the study of rocks called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Petrology**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Petrology**

 
 
• Petrology is the scientific study of rocks, encompassing their origin, composition, texture, and structure.
 
• It delves into the processes that form and transform rocks, such as igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary processes.
 
• Petrologists investigate the mineral composition of rocks, their physical properties, and the geological conditions under which they formed.
 
• This field plays a crucial role in understanding the Earth's history and the dynamics of geological processes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fruit Science (Pomology)**

 
 
• Pomology is the branch of horticulture that focuses on the cultivation, breeding, and study of fruits.
 
• It encompasses various aspects of fruit production, including tree and vine training, fruit quality assessment, disease and pest management, and the development of new fruit varieties.
 
• Pomology contributes to improving fruit production, enhancing fruit quality, and ensuring sustainable fruit cultivation practices.
 
 
 
• **Mycology**
 
 
• Mycology is the scientific study of fungi.
 
• It explores the biology, genetics, biochemistry, taxonomy, and ecology of fungi, which include yeasts, molds, and mushrooms.
 
• Mycology has significant implications in various fields, including medicine (antibiotics, immunology), agriculture (mycorrhizae, biocontrol agents), and industry (food production, bioremediation).
 
 
 
• **Soil Science (Pedology)**
 
 
• Soil science is the study of soil, its formation, properties, classification, and management.
 
• It investigates soil composition (minerals, organic matter), soil structure, soil water, soil fertility, and the impact of human activities on soil quality.
 
• Soil science is crucial for sustainable agriculture, environmental protection, and understanding the Earth's ecosystems.

questions.question: When does the entire earth experience equal days and nights?
questions.solution:
__
 
• On the **Day of equinox**__, the entire earth experience equal days and nights. 
 
• An equinox occurs when the plane of Earth's equator passes through the center of the Sun. It takes place twice in a year-March 21 and September 23. However, the dates can sometimes vary by a day or two because of difference in leap and non-leap years.
 
• **Winter Solstice**-It is the shortest period of daylight and longest night of the year. In this, the Earth's poles has its maximum tilt away from the Sun.
 
• It occurs twice a year. It occurs once in Northern Hemisphere and once in Southern Hemisphere.
 
• Northern Hemisphere Winter Solstice: 21st December, Southern Hemisphere Winter Solstice: 21st June. Again, the dates can sometimes vary by a day or two because of difference in leap and non-leap years.
 
• **Summer Solistice**-It is the longest period of daylight and shortest night of the year. In this, the Earth's poles has its maximum tilt towards the Sun. 
 
• It occurs twice a year. It occurs once in Northern Hemisphere and once in Southern Hemisphere.
 
• Northern Hemisphere Summer Solstice: 21st June, Southern Hemisphere Summer Solstice: 22nd December. Again, the dates can sometimes vary by a day or two because of difference in leap and non-leap years.

questions.question: Which are the two wettest places on Earth that receive more than 1,080 cm of rainfall in a year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cherrapunji and Mawsynram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Cherrapunji** and **Mawsynram** are located in the Indian state of Meghalaya.
 
• Both places experience heavy rainfall due to the orographic lift of moist air from the Bay of Bengal.
 
• **Mawsynram** holds the record for the highest average annual rainfall, which exceeds 1,080 cm.
 
• **Cherrapunji** is also known for its record-setting rainfall, often competing with Mawsynram for the title of the wettest place on Earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Orographic Rainfall**: This occurs when moist air is forced to rise over a mountain, cooling and condensing to form precipitation.
 
• **Meghalaya**: A state in northeastern India, known for its hilly terrain and significant rainfall.
 
• **Monsoon**: Seasonal winds that bring heavy rains, especially to the Indian subcontinent, crucial for agriculture but also causing floods.
 
• **Bay of Bengal**: A large water body in the northeastern part of the Indian Ocean, contributing to the moisture-laden winds that impact rainfall in Cherrapunji and Mawsynram.

questions.question: Where does the East Coast of India lie?

options.text: Between Gulf of Cambay and Cape Comorin
Between Eastern Ghats and the Bay of Bengal

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The East Coast of India lies between the Eastern Ghats mountain range and the Bay of Bengal.**
 
• **The Eastern Ghats, also known as the Mahendra Range**, is a discontinuous mountain range that runs parallel to the **East Coast of India**.
 
• It stretches along the states of** Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Tamil Nadu**.
 
• **The East Coast plains, **which lie between the** Eastern Ghats and the Bay of Bengal, **are relatively flat and fertile, making them suitable for agriculture.
 
• This region is home to several major cities and important ports along the coast.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Between the Gulf of Cambay and Cape Comorin lies the western coast of India, also known as the West Coast of India.**

 
 
• The West Coast of India is situated along the** Arabian Sea and extends from the Gulf of Cambay (also known as the Gulf of Khambhat) in the north to Cape Comorin (also known as Kanyakumari) in the south.**
 
• This coastal stretch includes the states of **Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, and Kerala.**
 
• **The West Coast of India** is known for its** beautiful beaches, diverse culture, and important port cities such as Mumbai, Mangalore, Kochi, and Thiruvananthapuram.**
 
 
 
• **Between Maharashtra and Kerala lies the state of Karnataka.**
 
 
• Karnataka is located on the southwestern part of India and shares its borders with **Maharashtra to the north and Kerala to the south.**
 
• The state capital of Karnataka is Bengaluru (Bangalore), which is known as the **technology hub of India.**
 
• Karnataka is known for its** rich cultural heritage, historical sites, and natural beauty**.
 
• It is also home to several important cities and tourist destinations, including **Mysore, Hampi, Mangalore, and Coorg.**
 
 
 
• **​Between Diu and Kerala lies the state of Gujarat and the Union Territory of Daman and Diu.**
 
 
• **Diu** is a small island and town located off the southern coast of **Gujarat, while Kerala is situated on the southwestern tip of India.**
 
• **To travel from Diu to Kerala, **one would need to traverse the state of **Gujarat, pass through Maharashtra, and then enter Kerala.**
 
• The journey would involve traveling along the western coast of India.

questions.question: Which of the following states is NOT a part of the Peninsular Plateau in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Peninsular Plateau** in India is a large region of elevated land that lies to the south of the** Indo-Gangetic Plain.**
 
• It is mainly composed of **Precambrian rocks** that are millions of years old.
 
• The plateau covers parts of several Indian states, including **Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Kerala.**
 
• However, **Punjab** is **not **a part of the Peninsular Plateau.
 
• It is located in the northwest of India and is mainly composed of **alluvial plains and river valleys.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Peninsular Plateau** is characterized by its composition of ancient** crystalline, igneous, and metamorphic** rocks.
 
• **Maharashtra** is a part of the Peninsular Plateau and includes the Deccan Plateau, which is a** large volcanic plateau** that covers much of central and southern India.
 
• **Madhya Pradesh **is also a part of the Peninsular Plateau and includes the **Vindhya and Satpura **mountain ranges, as well as parts of the Deccan Plateau.
 
• **Tamil Nadu** is a state in the south of India that is also a part of the Peninsular Plateau.
 
• It includes the **Eastern Ghats mountain range** and the **Nilgiri Hills.**
